papers.abstract_en: Quantum batteries are quantum systems that potentially serve as fuel for other quantum devices by receiving and supplying energy. In this work, we propose a theoretical scheme to enhance ergotropy and charging power of quantum Battery in the system under consideration through squeezed light. Moreover, The system comprises a coherently driven charger cavity, a strongly dissipative auxiliary cavity acting as a mediator, and an energy--storage battery cavity. Quantum nonreciprocity and directional energy flow are established via destructive quantum interference between the direct coupling path and the loss--engineered indirect path. A degenerate optical parametric amplifier integrated into the charger cavity acts as an active, phase--sensitive energy source that injects two--photon quantum excitations and anomalous correlations. Using a strictly open--quantum--system framework derived directly from the Lindblad master equation, we obtain the full expectation--value dynamics and stationary states. We show that active parametric driving drastically increases the stored energy and peak charging power while maintaining nonreciprocal energy trapping in the battery. We achieve a multi-order-of-magnitude boost in the battery's stored energy, charging power, and ergotropy. We also analyze the effects of pure dephasing on the charging power, ergotropy, and extractable work quality.. Although two--photon pumping introduces photon--number fluctuations that slightly lower the fractional ergotropy ratio ${\cal W}_{\rm B}/{\cal E}_{\rm B}$, the absolute extractable work remains substantially elevated compared to unassisted configurations.

papers.title_en: Lepton polarization and sensitivity to the form factors in $Λ\to p\,\ell^-\barν_\ell$ with lattice QCD
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the polarization of the charged lepton in the semileptonic hyperon decay $Λ\to p\,\ell^-\barν_\ell$ ($\ell=e,μ$) within the Standard Model, using the form factors obtained from lattice QCD. We compute the longitudinal, transverse and normal polarization of the lepton, the forward-backward asymmetry of each lepton spin state, and the lepton flavor universality ratio $R_{μe}$. We show that the longitudinal polarization determines the ratio $g_1/f_1$ of the axial-vector to vector couplings, and that the forward-backward asymmetries of the electron and of negative-helicity muons determine the weak magnetism. The asymmetry of positive-helicity muons is fixed by kinematics up to a small dependence on the second-class form factors, whereas $R_{μe}$ is nearly independent of $g_1/f_1$ and the weak magnetism. For comparison, we also use the QCD sum-rule form factors, whose $g_1/f_1$ and weak magnetism are opposite in sign to experiment and lattice QCD, and find very different values for the observables that depend on them. Moreover, the $q^2$ dependence of $R_{μe}$ fixes the longitudinal polarization of the muon, which can thus be measured from the decay rates, without measuring the muon spin. The normal polarization is generated by the electromagnetic final-state interaction and provides the Standard Model reference for searches for time-reversal violation. The electron forward-backward asymmetry and $R_{μe}$ can be measured at BESIII and the proposed Super Tau-Charm Facility, and $R_{μe}$ also at LHCb. These measurements can test the Standard Model and the lattice-QCD form factors.

papers.title_en: Midrapidity dip and limiting fragmentation of charged hadrons from RHIC to LHC energies
papers.abstract_en: The charged-hadron pseudorapidity density $\dndeta$ in central heavy-ion collisions has a midrapidity depression that deepens with collision energy. Whether it reflects structure in the rapidity density $\dndy$ or only the kinematics of the $y\toη$ transformation has mostly been argued with effective or model-based Jacobians. We test this without an event generator, with a $y\toη$ kernel built from measured identified-hadron spectra. In central Au+Au and Pb+Pb collisions from $\snn=19.6$~GeV to 5.36~TeV the data do not require a dip in $\dndy$: the decisive null-hypothesis family gives $p\ge\pMinAll$ in all variants. For dips up to one rapidity unit wide, the depth giving $p<0.05$ in half the pseudo-experiments is \rng{\dminLHClo}{\dminLHChi}% at the LHC and \rng{\dminRHIClo}{\dminRHIChi}% at 62.4--200~GeV. Generator closure tests show a false dip at top RHIC energy caused by the forward region. As the LHC data barely constrain the fragmentation region, an energy sum rule calibrated on RHIC data, with the RHIC shape of that region, gives best-fit LHC/RHIC ratios of \rng{\sLoE}{\sHiE}, \rng{\sLoF}{\sHiF} and \rng{\sLoG}{\sHiG} at 2.76, 5.02 and 5.36~TeV for three shape families, with 95% intervals over the families of \rng{\sNFLoE}{\sNFHiE}, \rng{\sNFLoF}{\sNFHiF} and \sNFG that include unity, although at 2.76 and 5.02~TeV the fits prefer \rng{\pullLoEF}{\pullHiEF}$\,σ$ more energy than calibrated. Over plausible RHIC covariances and kernels the best-fit ratios span \rng{\sSystAllLo}{\sSystAllHi}, and single variants exclude unity at \systUnionAbs: limiting fragmentation is neither established nor excluded.

papers.title_en: Distillable entanglement is continuous
papers.abstract_en: We prove continuity of distillable entanglement, the optimal asymptotic rate at which copies of a bipartite state can be converted into maximally entangled pairs by local operations and classical communication (LOCC) with vanishing error. We establish an explicit asymptotic continuity bound that holds for arbitrary bipartite states and depends logarithmically on the system dimension. This bound has the same structure as known continuity bounds for conditional entropy, entanglement cost, and relative entropy of entanglement. Our proof constructs an explicit LOCC protocol that converts either of two arbitrary bipartite states into the other at an ebit cost that vanishes as their trace distance tends to zero.

papers.title_en: Automatic indexing of wide-band quasi-Laue neutron diffraction patterns of large unit cells
papers.abstract_en: With a continuous spectrum of incident neutron wavelengths, quasi-Laue diffraction records many Bragg reflections from a stationary crystal, each satisfying the diffraction condition at a particular wavelength. Because the wavelength of each reflection is not measured, the crystal orientation must be determined from the scattering directions alone. At the new IMAGINE-X instrument, instant-readout detectors and many short exposures per experiment require this indexing to run automatically, yet for a protein crystal at the full 2-10 Angstrom band a single peak can have approximately $10^4$ candidate reflections, and a random orientation indexes a large fraction of the observed peaks. We describe an algorithm that indexes such patterns for a known unit cell and wavelength band. Differential evolution searches uniformly sampled rotations, matching observed directions to band-limited shells of candidate directions, and each solution is tested against the indexing expected for a random orientation. In a benchmark search, a k-d tree and a persistent pool of 32 worker processes reduce the wall time 270-fold relative to a serial scan of all candidates. The algorithm is first validated on the time-of-flight diffractometer MANDI, where the measured wavelengths give a reference solution by standard indexing. With the wavelengths discarded, every indexed reflection from 93 rare-earth garnet patterns agrees up to harmonic order. The algorithm then reliably indexes the natural mineral mesolite, measured on the original image plate at IMAGINE before the upgrade, and the protein T4 lysozyme, measured on the new IMAGINE-X instrument over the full band.

papers.title_en: Threshold effects of inelastic neutrino-dark-matter scattering in AGN spikes
papers.abstract_en: High-energy neutrinos from active galactic nuclei provide a powerful probe of dark matter (DM) spikes surrounding supermassive black holes. While elastic neutrino-DM scattering mediated by a light particle produces little net attenuation due to regeneration, inelastic scattering, $νχ_1\toνχ_2$, introduces a nonzero minimum energy loss, $E_{\rm th}$. We show that this threshold prevents the near-cancellation between attenuation and regeneration, producing a distinctive spectral deficit above $E_{\rm th}$ accompanied by a pile-up below it. Solving the full neutrino cascade, including repeated scattering and secondary neutrinos from excited-state decays, we demonstrate that this feature persists for both narrow and broad energy-transfer kernels. Using public IceCube data for NGC 1068 and an unbinned likelihood analysis with a freely fitted intrinsic power-law spectrum, we derive upper limits on the asymptotic optical depth of $τ_0<26-39$ for a narrow kernel (kernel width $ε=0.01$) over $E_{\rm th}=0.24-3.0$ TeV and $τ_0<20-26$ for a broad kernel ($ε=0.36$) over $E_{\rm th}=0.24-2.4$ TeV, at the nominal $90\%$ confidence level. An intrinsic high-energy cutoff weakens the narrow-kernel limits by factors of $2.2-7.4$ and the broad-kernel limits by factors of $2.0-5.0$. We further investigate DM velocity effects and combine NGC 1068 with CGCG 420-015 and TXS 0506+056 to extend the threshold reach. In a vector-mediator realization, an optimistic adiabatic DM spike can yield constraints on the neutrino coupling competitive with laboratory bounds for broad energy-transfer kernels.

papers.title_en: $κ$-Parametrized Boltzmann Distribution Sampling on Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
papers.abstract_en: Generative models use training data to produce new samples that resemble the original, with applications in classification and recommendation systems. Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) are at the core of generative models but suffer from the computational intractability of training, which relies on sampling an unknown Boltzmann Distribution (BD). The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can assist RBM training, potentially providing benefits over strictly classical strategies. One particular problem is determining the quantum circuit depth for an arbitrary problem size that yields the expected sampling results. In this study, we evaluate QAOA-assisted sampling of BDs using Qiskit's Aer Simulator by analysing the inverse effective temperature of the distribution, $κ$, for tractable problem sizes. The results provide numerical evidence, based on Qiskit Aer simulations, that parameterized annealing-scheduled QAOA (PAQ-QAOA) can approximate RBM Boltzmann sampling for the tractable instances considered, while hardware performance and scaling remain open questions.
authors: Neto, João Marcos Cavalcanti de Albuquerque

papers.title_en: Direct measurement of the ${}^{23}\mathrm{Mg}(p, γ){}^{24}\mathrm{Al}$ reaction using the DRAGON recoil separator and a hybrid array of $γ$-ray detectors
papers.abstract_en: Background: The $^{23}$Mg$(p,γ)^{24}$Al reaction plays a key role in nova nucleosynthesis, serving as a bridge between the Ne-Na and Mg-Al cycles and impacting synthesis of a wide variety of nuclides. It is crucial that the rate of this reaction be well constrained by experimental data, in particular the properties of the key resonance at $E_{\mathrm{cm}}\approx480$ keV, which dominates the rate at nova temperatures. Purpose: Our study aims to improve experimental constraints on the energy and strength of the key $E_{\mathrm{cm}}\approx480$ keV $^{23}$Mg$(p,γ)^{24}$Al resonance through a new direct measurement of its strength and energy. Methods: We used a $^{23}\mathrm{Mg}$ radioactive beam to directly observe capture into the $E_{\mathrm{cm}}\approx480$ keV resonance in inverse kinematics. The $^{24}\mathrm{Al}$ recoils were selected by the DRAGON recoil separator, and coincident $γ$ rays were measured in a hybrid $\mathrm{LaBr}_3/\mathrm{CeBr}_3/\mathrm{BGO}$ scintillator array. The $^{24}\mathrm{Al}$ singles yield was used to determine the resonance strength, while the time difference between the coincident $γ$ rays and the incident beam was used to determine the resonance energy. Results: We obtained a strength of $ωγ=38(7)$ meV and an energy of $E_{\mathrm{cm}}=478.8(26)$ keV for the key astrophysical $^{23}\mathrm{Mg}(p,γ)^{24}\mathrm{Al}$ resonance. Conclusions: Our reported strength is in excellent agreement with the previously reported direct measurement, as well as shell model calculations. Our energy is in good agreement with earlier indirect measurements. Reaction rate calculations incorporating our results indicate that the $^{23}\mathrm{Mg}(p,γ)^{24}\mathrm{Al}$ rate is constrained to a $1σ$ up/down factor of 1.5 or smaller in the nova temperature range of 0.2--0.4 GK.

papers.title_en: Sparse Carleman Embeddings for Nonlinear Discrete Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract_en: Discrete nonlinear dynamical systems arise in population models, iterative optimization, and numerical simulations, where computing many iterations can be costly in high dimensions. We study Carleman embedding for forced quadratic discrete systems and its application to quantum state preparation. Under explicit stability and initial-state assumptions, we prove that the truncation error decreases geometrically with the embedding degree, uniformly over all iterations. A central obstacle in discrete time is that the lifted update can become dense even when the original coefficient maps are sparse. We overcome this obstacle by constructing an exact auxiliary linear-system representation that applies the coefficient maps one tensor factor at a time, with row and column sparsities bounded independently of the truncation degree. After rescaling, the associated history system has a condition number that grows linearly with the iteration count, uniformly in the truncation degree. These results yield a quantum algorithm for preparing an approximation to the normalized $n$th iterate with constant success probability. Under coherent input-access assumptions, and for fixed sparsity, stability parameters, and a known positive lower bound on the final-state norm, the oracle query complexity is linear in $n$ and polylogarithmic in the inverse accuracy. Numerical experiments in one and three dimensions illustrate the convergence of the truncated embedding.

papers.title_en: Decoding with alternating weighted graph sparsification for quantum low-density parity-check codes
papers.abstract_en: Real-time decoding is a fundamental necessity for building fault-tolerant quantum computers. In this work, we introduce decoding with alternating weighted graph sparsification (DAWG), an ensemble based approach that combines Tanner graph sparsification with ensembling belief-propagation (BP) decoders. The DAWG decoder runs BP decoders over the full detector error model Tanner graph for certain iterations to then transfer the posteriors to a sparsified graph in which additional rounds of BP are run. Each of the decoders in the ensemble uses a different transfer matrix to map the posterior information to the sparsified graph. We use the serial schedule for the minimum-sum BP decoders and, thus, employ Vibe decoding ideas by randomizing the schedules of each of them. The performance of the DAWG decoder is then numerically studied for bivariate bicycle codes and superdense color code circuits to be compared with other state-of-the-art decoding approaches. Importantly, the DAWG decoder shows a similar performance to Relay belief-propagation and Vibe decoding when combined with an order-$0$ Localized Statistics Decoding (LSD-$0$) post-processor. Crucially, the post-processor is called an order of magnitude less times than for Vibe with the same ensemble size, indicating that the introduced latency tail will be minimal. Furthermore, LSD-$0$ operates on a sparsified decoding graph of a fraction of the size of the full detector error model, which simplifies the resources required by specialized hardware to support it. Overall, the DAWG+LSD-$0$ decoder represents a viable low-cost BP-based decoding algorithm for quantum error correction codes.

papers.title_en: Nuclear recoil effects with a realistic nuclear charge form factor
papers.abstract_en: We introduce a novel two-parameter Gamma model of the nuclear charge distribution as an alternative to the widely used Fermi distribution. The model yields simple analytical formulas for all moments of the charge distribution and closed-form expressions for the electrostatic potential and momentum-space form factor, the latter satisfying the correct analyticity requirements for a physical charged particle. We apply the model to calculate the nuclear recoil correction to the Lamb shift in electronic and muonic atoms and analyze its nuclear-model dependence. We find that the nuclear-size recoil corrections to energy levels of heavy muonic atoms are strongly sensitive to higher moments of the nuclear charge distribution, highlighting the importance of realistic nuclear modeling. To facilitate further calculations, we also provide the Fortran code RECFNS, designed for computing the nuclear recoil correction within the QED framework. The present work establishes a basis for future extensions to higher orders in the electron-to-nucleus mass ratio, hyperfine splitting, and radiative corrections.

papers.title_en: Interference-induced dynamical crossovers in quantum walks on disordered square lattices
papers.abstract_en: We study discrete-time quantum walks with Fourier, Grover, and Hadamard coin operators on disordered square lattices, alongside classical random walks. Edges in the lattice are absent with a probability, $p$. In this case, both classical and quantum walks exhibit an essentially identical degradation of transport. We then study a general version of this model, in which the existing edges are retained. However, the absent edges are no longer absent, but now become partially transmitting, with a transmission coefficient $f$. We find that the response is now quite sensitive to the walk protocol and coin symmetry. The classical walk exhibits asymptotic stability of the anomalous diffusion exponent, $β(t)$. In comparison, quantum walks exhibit a monotonically decaying $β(t)$ beyond the initial transient regime, leading to the absence of quantum diffusion in two dimensions. We map the transport regimes in the $(f,p)$ plane and identify the contour for $β=1$, which separates the subdiffusive and superdiffusive regimes. We also examine the effective diffusion coefficient, the inverse participation ratio, and the first two moments of edge transmission. We restrict ourselves to analyzing bulk propagation prior to finite-size boundary reflections. The results indicate that quantum transport depends significantly on coin-specific interference and cannot be fully described by transmission statistics alone.

papers.title_en: The neutrino fog for inelastic dark matter
papers.abstract_en: We characterize the behavior of the neutrino fog for inelastic dark matter scattering on xenon. The inelastic scattering kinematics reshape the recoil spectrum of the signal and produce a qualitatively different neutrino fog landscape. In some regions of the inelastic parameter space the fog is completely absent for future xenon experiments at any scale, while in other regions the fog is dispelled only to reappear at larger exposures. We find that multiple background sources with uncertain normalizations can make the onset of the fog jump discontinuously with the dark matter mass and mass splitting, while the discovery limit varies smoothly. We also describe a mechanism by which reduced uncertainties on neutrino rates may have the unintuitive effect of raising neutrino floors derived from the fog opacity.

papers.title_en: Annealed sampling of diffusion models in lattice field theory
papers.abstract_en: Machine learning methods have recently gained increasing interest as possible means of solving critical slowing down in lattice field theory, with particular emphasis on sampling methods using field transformations such as normalizing flows, annealing/out-of-equilibrium methods, and diffusion models. Annealing methods provide appealing polynomial scaling and exactness guarantees, while diffusion models use a simple and efficient score-matching training procedure. This work explores a method combining these benefits, first training an energy-based diffusion model using score matching, then sampling using either stochastic normalizing flows (SNFs) or flow-transformed replica exchange (T-REX). The choice of sampling method can be made after training the diffusion model; the theoretical properties of SNFs and T-REX and their relative trade-offs are discussed. Numerical results are presented for scalar field theory and the O(3) non-linear sigma model, using a class of local-footprint energy models with efficient gradient and divergence calculations. Sampling from the trained models follows predicted exactness and scaling properties, and significantly improves over sampling methods without a learned component.

papers.title_en: Network nonlocality with tripartite entangled sources
papers.abstract_en: Quantum networks are built from independent sources, and their nonlocality has mostly been studied with sources that emit bipartite entangled states. A source of three entangled qubits is richer, since its nonlocality can be tested by the Mermin or the more demanding Svetlichny inequality. We ask how network nonlocality relates to these two single-source notions and find that the answer depends on the wiring. When two central nodes without inputs share every source, Bell-state measurements turn every Svetlichny violation into a network violation, and even all entangled generalised Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger states violate the network inequality. When a single central node is shared, the relation reverses, and a network violation requires a Mermin violation of the source. With more sources, the maximal violation depends on whether their number is even or odd, and we give tight bounds for both cases. These results show that the way multipartite sources are wired decides which kind of nonlocality a network inherits.

papers.title_en: Holographic Approaches to Hadron Structure
papers.abstract_en: We give an introduction to and an overview of holographic approaches to QCD and hadron structure. After an introduction to the string-theoretic foundations of holographic QCD, we review the predictions of top-down and bottom-up models for the phenomenology of mesons, baryons, and glueballs. We focus on the top-down model following from probe flavor branes in the Witten model of low-energy Yang-Mills theory and, in the more phenomenological approach of bottom-up models, on minimal models based on five-dimensional anti-de Sitter space.

papers.title_en: Modeling the CNOT gate in Germanium double quantum dots
papers.abstract_en: We model a controlled-NOT (CNOT) gate mediated by exchange interactions in a realistic Ge/GeSi hole spin-qubit device. We use for that purpose a computationally efficient framework based on a compact dressed basis of many-body singlet and triplet states, which enables fast time-dependent simulations that would be prohibitive within a conventional configuration-interaction approach. We discuss the dominant sources of infidelity in ideal (noise-free) devices. On the one hand, the nonadiabaticity of the tunnel barrier ramps, enhanced by the transverse component of the exchange interaction, imposes limits on the speed of the CNOT gate. On the other hand, the AC Stark shift of the conditional resonance and the off-resonant driving of the complementary transition can significantly degrade the gate fidelity and call for a careful optimization of the driving conditions. Finally, we investigate the impact of quasi-static charge noise on the fidelity of the CNOT gate. We find that the capture of charges near the qubits can strongly disrupt the conditional operation, while the nanometer-scale motion of charges results in a loss of fidelity that sensitively depends on the position and strength of the corresponding dipole. Our results quantify the requirements on barrier control, microwave driving, and charge-noise stability for high-fidelity two-qubit operations in Ge/GeSi hole-spin qubits.

papers.title_en: Photoproduction of <math><mrow><msup><mi>K</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></math> off protons in the resonance region
papers.abstract_en: We analyze the <math><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></math> process in the resonance region within the framework of the isobar model. The amplitude is constructed as a sum of tree-level Feynman diagrams with the addition of the contact current ensuring gauge invariance of the total amplitude. The resonance content of our models is inspired by a model for the isospin-related <math><mrow><msup><mi>K</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msup></mrow></math> channel. The main coupling constant in the <math><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> vertex is estimated with the help of isospin symmetry, and the rest of the free parameters (resonance couplings and hadronic form-factor cutoffs) are calibrated to the available <math><mrow><msup><mi>K</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></math> data. Using the resulting models, we calculate the differential and total cross sections as well as polarization observables <math><mo>(</mo><mi>P</mi></math>, <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></math>, <math><mi>T</mi></math>, <math><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>x</mi></msub></math>, <math><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></math>, and compare them with measurements. We identify the <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1720</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1900</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></math> states as the most important ones for good correspondence with the experimental data.

papers.title_en: Finite-data certification of mixed-state nonstabilizerness from Pauli witnesses
papers.abstract_en: We apply Hoeffding's inequality directly to weighted estimators of Pauli-expanded witnesses to obtain finite-sample tests for mixed-state nonstabilizerness. With witnesses and shot allocations fixed in advance, the tests control false positives under independent sampling. We also derive sufficient shot counts for a specified positive violation margin and target detection probability. A separate plug-in Gaussian diagnostic is used for comparison. Examples include the single-qubit stabilizer-octahedron criterion, a fixed two-qubit Pauli-correlation Triangle witness, and a previously proposed two-copy Clifford circuit with postselection. For this circuit, we construct eight linear contrasts of the four-qubit input state for each prescribed output threshold. When the postselection probability is positive, the threshold is exceeded if and only if at least one contrast is positive. These contrasts involve 31 nonidentity Pauli observables covered by 15 local product-Pauli bases. Using independent measurement batches, we obtain ratio-free threshold tests and explicit sufficient bounds on shots and input copies. For two identical, independent copies of a two-qubit state, we establish a sharp upper bound on the unnormalized contrast margin at the thresholds considered. An explicit state family attains every positive margin up to this bound. Finite-shot simulations assess detection probabilities for a bound-attaining input and its noisy extension. Separate null checks cover boundary and interior states, as well as inputs with zero postselection probability.

papers.title_en: Adaptive stabilizer-state-fidelity certification
papers.abstract_en: Certifying the fidelity of a prepared state to a target stabilizer state is a fundamental task in quantum information processing. The reference [Phys. Rev. A 99, 042337 (2019)] gave the optimal worst-case lower bound from one fixed stabilizer generator gauge, but gauge dependence can leave a large fidelity ambiguity. We develop an adaptive extension that reports the full certified fidelity interval. First, for a single gauge, we derive the complementary optimal worst-case upper bound. We then formulate gauge selection as an adaptive design problem in which each round solves endpoint linear programs and chooses a new gauge by a witness elimination policy. We prove monotonic tightening, simultaneous finite-shot coverage with an explicit uncertainty floor, exact recovery once all nontrivial stabilizers are covered, and the worst-case necessity of full coverage. Finally, we identify affine-subspace-supported syndrome distributions for which adaptivity can beat this exponential benchmark, and we numerically confirm faster concentration.

papers.title_en: Local correlation formula based on the liquid-drop model for the energy released in proton radioactivity
papers.abstract_en: Based on the liquid-drop model, we propose and refine a local formula for the released energy of proton radioactivity <math><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></math>. The calculated results for 44 proton emitters with 71 <math><mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>≤</mo></mrow></math> 91 are in good agreement with the experimental data. For comparison, the WS4 [Phys. Lett. B 734, 215 (2014)] and FRDM [At. Data Nucl. Data Tables 125, 1 (2019)] nuclear mass models are also employed. The root-mean-square (rms) deviations between the experimental data and theoretical results obtained from this work, WS4, and FRDM are 0.071 MeV, 0.144 MeV, and 0.348 MeV, respectively. These results demonstrate that the present approach reproduces the experimental <math><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></msub></math> values well in the considered region. The formula is further employed to predict the released energies for candidate proton emitters, and the predictions are broadly consistent with those of the other models.

papers.title_en: Ergotropy activation and coherence in dissipatively charged quantum batteries
papers.abstract_en: Quantum batteries can exploit quantum resources to enhance energy storage and work extraction, and recent experimental progress has brought their implementation closer to reality. In realistic settings, however, environmental dissipation is unavoidable, making dissipative charging a physically relevant operating regime. Here, we investigate ergotropy in dissipatively charged quantum batteries, focusing on interaction-induced work extraction. For two coupled two-level systems (TLSs), we derive exact analytical expressions for the total, coherent, and incoherent ergotropy in both resonant and detuned configurations. We show that in the resonant case, ergotropy is activated only above a critical coupling associated with an interaction-induced energy-level crossing, whereas detuning enables ergotropy already in the weak-coupling regime. Moreover, quantum coherence, although necessary for coherent work extraction, is not by itself sufficient to guarantee nonzero coherent ergotropy. In the strong-coupling regime, the resonant setup reaches the maximum ergotropy at a finite coupling strength, whereas the detuned setup approaches the same limit only asymptotically. Extending the analysis to a periodic <math><mrow><mi mathvariant="italic">XX</mi></mrow></math> spin chain of <math><mi>N</mi></math> TLSs, we analytically derive the finite-temperature coupling threshold for ergotropy activation and show that it scales as <math><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> in the large-<math><mi>N</mi></math> limit. These results identify frequency detuning, interaction strength, and system size as key control parameters for ergotropy generation in open quantum batteries.

papers.title_en: Wave Is All You Need: A Quantum Language Model Based on Fully Connected Quantum Boltzmann Machine
papers.abstract_en: This work proposes a self-attention mechanism based on the fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine (FC-QBM), and further constructs a fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine language model (FC-QBM-LM) using the mechanism as the core engine. By performing unitary evolution on semantic quantum states, the mechanism implicitly implements positional encoding and self-attention computation, eliminating the need to decompose continuous semantic streams into discrete matrices for explicit matrix multiplication, with the measurement results naturally satisfying the normalization condition. Specifically, this work rigorously derives the computational principle of the self-attention mechanism based on FC-QBM, and demonstrates that this mechanism is mathematically equivalent to the classical self-attention mechanism. The mathematical principles governing the training and generation of FC-QBM-LM are thoroughly derived, and the two corresponding algorithms are subsequently developed. An 8-qubit FC-QBM-LM is finally constructed and trained on the corpus of Tang poetry. Under the 8-qubit setting, the quantum layer implements the entire positional encoding and self-attention computation pipeline with only 44 parameters. In the noiseless scenario, the model exhibits favorable convergence. Furthermore, the quantum circuit proposed in this work, which terminates with Y-axis rotation gates, achieves better convergence than the counterpart terminating with X-axis rotation gates. Under the small-sample regime and across eight distinct noise intensity levels, the model demonstrates strong noise robustness, retaining over 99% of its noiseless convergence performance. Experiments on five-character quatrain generation reveal that the model preliminarily exhibits three core capabilities: associative and divergent thinking, content generation across imagery and human-aligned word ordering.

papers.title_en: A Reduction Bound for Entanglement Detection by Positive Free Maps
papers.abstract_en: Collins, Hayden, and Nechita used free probability to construct families of $k$-positive but not $(k+1)$-positive maps and applied them to entanglement detection. We prove that positive free maps associated with compactly supported freely infinitely divisible distributions are no stronger than the reduction criterion in every ancillary dimension. In particular, these maps cannot detect positive partial transpose entanglement. The proof combines a joint Fock realization with an operator positivity certificate derived from free Lévy data.

papers.title_en: Boundary-condition independence of infinite-chain ground states in the $S=1$$J$-$D$ antiferromagnetic chain
papers.abstract_en: Extending the analytic machinery and using the numerical inputs from OpenAI's proofs of the Haldane gap, we study infinite-chain ground states of the $S=1$$J$-$D$ antiferromagnetic model $H=\sum_j\{\boldsymbol S_j\cdot\boldsymbol S_{j+1}+D(S_j^{\mathrm z})^2\}$ for sufficiently small $|D|$. We consider two finite-volume settings: periodic chains with an even number of sites, and open chains with an odd number of sites and the same positive magnetic field in the $\mathrm z$ direction at both endpoints. We prove that the ground states in each setting have an infinite-chain limit along the full sequence, without passing to a subsequence, and that the two limiting states coincide. Convergence is uniform in $D$ on a fixed neighborhood of zero. The common limit is a symmetric locally-unique gapped ground state, and its local expectation values depend continuously on $D$. These conclusions concern the two specified constructions, not uniqueness among all infinite-chain ground states. They provide the input for the study of a topological phase transition in a forthcoming revision of our companion paper. The author formulated the problem and proposed the basic strategy. ChatGPT Astra made substantial contributions to the inductive estimates and to completing the proof.

papers.title_en: Path integral control in the complex plane
papers.abstract_en: Path integral control is a stochastic optimal control framework that computes optimal policies as weighted averages over state trajectories. It was recently shown that, combined with stochastic quantum trajectories, the path integral control approach constitutes a promising alternative for quantum optimal control. In this work, we propose an extension of path integral control to the complex plane using circular complex Wiener processes. The change of measure is defined on the driving noise space under an exact control-noise matching condition, which also accommodates rank-deficient state diffusions. Applied to stochastic Schrödinger equations, the resulting formalism gives a compact treatment of paired non-Hermitian jump channels with unequal positive dissipation rates and yields cross-entropy-optimal feedback and open-loop control formulas.

papers.title_en: Rigorous Lower Bounds for Atomic and Ionic Ground-State Energies
papers.abstract_en: We establish a new iterative method for computing rigorous lower bounds for the ground-state energies of all atoms and ions. The accuracy of the resulting bounds depends on two ingredients: the quality of the initial energy estimate and the quality of the used upper bound for the maximum number of bound electrons, $N_c(Z)$, as a function of the nuclear charge $Z>0$. In particular, this new method allows us to establish the explicit lower bound $E(N,Z) \geq -0.8710\,N^{1/3}Z^2$ for the ground-state energy $E(N,Z)$ of the atom/ion with $N \in \mathbb{N}$ electrons and nuclear charge $Z \in (0,N]$, thereby considerably improving the best known constant $A=(3/2)^{1/3} \approx 1.1447$ in the estimate $E(N,Z) \geq -A\,N^{1/3}Z^2$ for $0 < Z \leq N$ and coming much closer to the best possible constant given by the Thomas-Fermi asymptotics $\lim_{N \to \infty} |E(N,N)|N^{-7/3}= -E_{\text{TF}}(1)\approx 0.7687$ derived in Adv. Math., 23(1) by Lieb and Simon. To demonstrate the potential and the limits of our method, we also compute explicit lower bounds for the ground-state energies $E(N,N)$ of all atoms with $2 \leq N \leq 86$ and we compare them with the bounds obtained in J. Chem. Phys., 62(8) by Hertel, Lieb, Thirring and the bounds obtained by Seco in his dissertation. Finally, we also provide a uniqueness result for the expectation values of the kinetic, potential and interaction energies on the ground-state space.

papers.title_en: The effective mass of the Pauli-Fierz electron: a cutoff-independent lower bound and the breakdown of mass renormalization
papers.abstract_en: We consider the Pauli-Fierz model of one spinless non-relativistic electron coupled to the quantized transverse electromagnetic field, without external potential, with a sharp ultraviolet cutoff Lambda and bare mass m. Let h = m_eff/m be the ratio of the effective mass, defined by the curvature of the fiber ground state energy at total momentum zero, to the bare mass; by scaling, h depends only on the fine structure constant alpha = e^2/(4 pi) and on lambda = Lambda/m. We prove two lower bounds. First, h >= 1 + 0.3441 alpha/(1 + 0.2985 sqrt(alpha) + 0.1252 alpha) for all alpha > 0 and all lambda >= 1; the bound does not depend on the cutoff, and with the band extended to the cutoff its first order coefficient in alpha is the perturbative one of Hiroshima and Spohn. The proof uses a coherent translation of the field applied to the ground state as a trial state; the term linear in the translation vanishes by minimality of the ground state. Second, for every fixed alpha, h grows faster than linearly: for every epsilon > 0, h >= lambda^(8/7 - epsilon) for all large lambda (8/7 is the limit of the method). Consequently iota_PF(alpha) := inf_{lambda > 0} h/lambda > 0, and for a fixed physical mass m_phys a bare mass reproducing it exists only if Lambda <= m_phys/iota_PF(alpha). This was expected, but not proved, by Lieb and Loss (2002). The proof of the second bound starts from the sharp self-energy asymptotics of a companion paper and uses a trial state obtained from the ground state by a phase depending on the field configuration. The new ingredients are an estimator for the position of the electron given by the local centre of a shallow level set of the photon cloud, the decoupling of a localized part of the field from the electron through a divergence-free external subspace, and a proof that shallow depressions near the edge of the localization window are rare.

papers.title_en: The Genus-One B-Model Calabi-Yau/Landau-Ginzburg Correspondence
papers.abstract_en: Let $f:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $n$ with an isolated critical point at the origin. The Calabi--Yau/Landau--Ginzburg correspondence predicts a close relation between invariants of the Landau--Ginzburg orbifold $(\mathbb C^n/\mathbb Z_n,f)$ and those of the associated Calabi--Yau hypersurface $ X_f=\{[z_1:\cdots:z_n]\in\mathbb P^{n-1}:f(z_1,\ldots,z_n)=0\}. $ In this paper, we establish this correspondence for the genus-one B-model by constructing the Landau--Ginzburg genus-one B-model invariant intrinsically from the $f$-twisted Laplacian on $\mathbb{C}^n/\mathbb{Z}_n$ and proving that it agrees with the corresponding BCOV invariant of $X_f$ up to an additive constant depending only on the dimension.

papers.title_en: Resource-Optimal Screening for Two-Tier Quantum System Characterization
papers.abstract_en: Quantum processing units (QPUs) require frequent benchmarking to track hardware drift, yet standard protocols such as randomized benchmarking are resource-intensive and compete with application workloads for scarce QPU time. We present a resource-optimal screening strategy that combines a two-tier, risk-based testing architecture with optimal experiment design: a lightweight screening probe runs regularly and triggers expensive full characterization only when statistically significant change is detected, while the probe itself is designed to maximize detection sensitivity under explicit resource constraints. For an exponential fidelity model, we derive closed-form optimal circuit sizes and introduce an effective gate count that renders the analysis hardware-independent. We instantiate the strategy for two applications. For gate-quality verification, we show that optimally designed screening probes outperform randomized benchmarking with optimal experimental design (OED) by more than 4$\times$ in detection rate at equal resource cost. For compiler benchmarking, we formalize compiler comparison as a paired hypothesis test and derive the optimal circuit size for distinguishing compilation strategies. Despite their different observables and test statistics, both applications yield structurally the same closed-form expression for the optimal probe circuit size as a function of gate fidelity, illustrating the generality of the framework. Numerical and hardware experiments on QPUs (Rigetti Ankaa-3, IQM Garnet, IQM Emerald) confirm the theoretical predictions, with observed optimal circuit sizes matching the derived values across all devices.

papers.title_en: Nucleon polarizabilities revisited: insights from the Bernabéu-Ericson-Ferro Fontan-Tarrach sum rule
papers.abstract_en:
We present a complete dispersive evaluation of the Bernabéu-Ericson-Ferro Fontan-Tarrach (BEFT) sum rule for the nucleon dipole polarizability difference $α_{E1}-β_{M1}$. The analysis is based on hyperbolic dispersion relations, which separate the $s$- and $t$-channel contributions without double counting and are particularly suited to backward real Compton scattering. This framework makes it possible to precisely determine the polarizability difference from independent dispersive input rather than from fits to low-energy Compton scattering data. The $s$-channel part is updated with modern single-pion photoproduction multipoles and model estimates of non-$πN$ inelastic channels. For the $t$-channel, we use contemporary dispersive input for $γγ\toππ/K\bar K_{I_t=0}$ together with Roy-Steiner equation solutions for $ππ/K\bar K_{I_t=0}\to N\bar N$, and we extend the calculation to the isovector $πη/K\bar K_{I_t=1}$ channel associated with the $a_0(980)$. The resulting treatment resolves the long-standing puzzle of earlier BEFT evaluations driven by the scalar-isoscalar two-pion channel and gives a controlled estimate of the subleading isovector contribution. Combining the resulting BEFT values with the Baldin sum rule, we obtain, in units of $10^{-4}\,\mathrm{fm}^3$, 
\[ α_{E1}^p=11.17(52),\quad β_{M1}^p=2.84(52),\quad α_{E1}^n=12.18(59),\quad β_{M1}^n=3.03(59). \]
 For the proton, these values provide a benchmark with a precision comparable to state-of-the-art dispersive and chiral effective field theory extractions. For the neutron, whose polarizabilities are much less directly constrained experimentally, the result provides an independent dispersive benchmark with an uncertainty comparable to that of the proton.

papers.title_en: Quantum neuroplastic learning for time-series processing
papers.abstract_en: Quantum machine learning uses quantum states and dynamics to represent and process data. In quantum reservoir computing, the physical system is typically fixed and a classical readout is trained. Inspired by the formation, strengthening and pruning of synapses during biological learning, we propose quantum neuroplastic learning (QNL), which reorganizes the couplings among the qubits of a quantum reservoir, much as experience rewires connections among neurons. Eligibility traces guide local edits to couplings, fields, gate angles and evolution time, and an edit is retained when a statistical bound on its improvement exceeds a complexity cost. We evaluate QNL under restarting and online monitored protocols on short- and long-term memory, nonlinear autoregressive processing and forecasting, and channel equalization tasks. In simulation, QNL enhances memory capacity, develops long-term recall and sustains adaptation across multiple tasks, with the largest benefit for tasks that require extended memory. On the IBM superconducting processor \texttt{ibm\_fez}, with six seven-qubit reservoirs running in parallel on 42 qubits (1.28 million shots in total), configurations learned in simulation and frozen before execution reduced the channel-equalization symbol error rate from 9.7% to 2.2% and achieved a lower error rate than a matched-budget tuned baseline.

papers.title_en: Remembering Brown-Rho scaling
papers.abstract_en: The properties of hadrons in dense matter have been a core interest of mine since I entered graduate school at Stony Brook in 1984. This interest was shaped both by the strong research activity on the subject at Stony Brook at the time and by the influence of Mannque Rho, who was a frequent visitor there. In this memoir dedicated to Mannque, I describe a selection of his works that sparked my interest in the subject and present my current perspective on what Mannque, together with Gerry Brown, sought to emphasize in the often-misinterpreted Brown--Rho scaling. In light of recent developments, I also discuss refinements of Brown--Rho scaling for mesons and baryons, associated with spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking and $U_A(1)$-breaking effects.

papers.title_en: Two exact quantum queries use at most six variables
papers.abstract_en: We give a direct analytic proof that every total Boolean function computable exactly with at most two quantum queries depends on at most six input variables. This bound is sharp. A previous derivation relied on a numerical classification of Boolean functions on at most four variables; to the best of our knowledge, ours is the first unconditional proof. The main difficulty beyond the one-query case is that query-path vectors need not be mutually orthogonal, so interference prevents the scalar weight-counting argument from applying. We overcome this difficulty by establishing a rigid support-and-branch decomposition: after the coordinates in the first-query support are fixed, the second query induces a family of exact one-query branches. This structural description may be of independent interest.

papers.title_en: Inferring Nuclear Radial Parameters from Initial-State Information in Heavy-Ion Collisions Using Deep Neural Networks
papers.abstract_en: The geometric structure of atomic nuclei plays an important role in shaping the initial conditions of high-energy nuclear collisions and the subsequent evolution of the quark--gluon plasma. In this work, we develop a multimodal deep-learning framework to infer the Woods--Saxon radius ($R_0$) and diffuseness parameter ($a$) from initial-state information. Using the TRENTo model for relativistic $^{238}$U+$^{238}$U collisions, we construct a dataset covering multiple combinations of $R_0$ and $a$, and perform parameter regression by combining two-dimensional entropy-density distributions with event-level scalar observables, including multiplicity and eccentricities $\varepsilon_2$--$\varepsilon_5$. The results show that the proposed framework can effectively recover the Woods--Saxon parameters from initial-state information. Joint multi-event inputs suppress statistical fluctuations and improve regression performance by enhancing the extraction of collective information. The inversion accuracy exhibits a pronounced centrality dependence: $R_0$ is best constrained in central collisions, whereas $a$ shows the strongest sensitivity in the mid-peripheral region and becomes less well constrained in ultra-central and peripheral collisions. These findings indicate that the initial-state geometry retains useful information about nuclear radial structure and provide a baseline for future studies that incorporate transport evolution and experimental final-state observables.

papers.title_en: Radiative Higgs decay to $ψ\left(4230\right)$
papers.abstract_en: We calculate the decay rate for the radiative Higgs decay $H \to ψ(4230) + γ$ within and beyond the SM. The vector state $ψ(4230)$ is a candidate exotic tetraquark state and has the quantum numbers $I^G(J^{PC})=0^-(1^{--})$, having a mass $m_{ψ(4230)}=4221.7 \pm 2.5$ MeV and a decay width $Γ_{ψ(4230)}=51 \pm 7$ MeV. We propose a practical parametrization of the so-called {\it direct amplitude}, using the leptonic coupling of the $ψ(4230)$ to estimate the short-distance overlap relevant to the Higgs decay amplitude. We find ${\cal B}_{\rm SM}( H \to ψ(4230) γ)=4.88^{+4.71}_{-4.52}\times 10^{-7}$, where the uncertainties are dominated by the experimental uncertainty in the leptonic decay width of the $ψ(4230)$. The branching ratio increases to about $10^{-6}$ for $y_c=-3 $, where $y_c$ is the Higgs-Yukawa coupling of the charm quark.

papers.title_en: Observation of measurement-induced localization phenomena in a solid-state spin system
papers.abstract_en: Quantum measurement can profoundly impact the dynamics of many-body systems, for instance, inducing phase transitions from volume-law chaotic phases to area-law localized phases. While chaotic phases emerge naturally in generic many-body systems, the experimental realization of a fully localized phase driven by measurement remains challenging, primarily owing to the stringent requirement of near-perfect isolation of the system from environmental dissipation. Here we experimentally observe measurement-induced localization phenomena in an interacting $^{13}\mathrm{C}$ nuclear spin system in diamond. In contrast to previous circuit-model-based experiments, our well-isolated system evolves under a physical many-body Hamiltonian with measurements intervening at intervals. By implementing either projective measurements on a single spin or global weak measurements on the entire system, we observe substantially prolonged spin autocorrelation times as the measurement frequency increases. Our results, combined with numerical simulations, provide evidence that quantum measurement can drive a many-body system into a localized regime, and lay the groundwork for future experimental investigations into measurement-induced many-body dynamics and related entanglement phenomena.

papers.title_en: Search for the rare decay $η^{\prime}\to 3γ$
papers.abstract_en: Using a data sample of $(10087 \pm 44) \times 10^{6} J/ψ$ events collected with the BESIII detector, we search for the rare decay $η^{\prime}\to 3γ$ via the process $J/ψ\toγη^{\prime}$. No significant signal is observed and an upper limit on the branching fraction of $η^{\prime}\to 3γ$ is set at $\mathcal{B}(η^{\prime}\to 3γ) < 2.25\times 10^{-5}$ at the 90% confidence level. This result improves the previous upper limit by more than a factor of four.

papers.title_en: Feasibility of Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing: From Quantum Links to Algorithms
papers.abstract_en: Practical fault-tolerant quantum computation requires a large number of physical qubits, posing a major challenge for scaling up individual quantum processors. Distributed architectures offer a promising solution by interconnecting multiple processors through quantum networks. However, remote Bell-pair generation remains technically demanding, making it essential to assess computational performance under limited communication resources. In this work, we present a comprehensive resource analysis of distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation using superconducting processors connected by microwave or optical links. We show that even a single physical communication channel per node can substantially reduce the physical-qubit requirements per node under experimentally motivated, forward-looking microwave-link assumptions of a 1 MHz physical Bell-pair generation rate and 90% fidelity, although at the cost of a roughly tenfold increase in execution time. Conversely, reducing the execution-time overhead requires substantially greater communication resources, including higher Bell-pair fidelities and extensive multiplexing. These results demonstrate the potential feasibility of distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation with limited communication resources and provide a quantitative basis for balancing quantum-link performance, processor size, and execution time.

papers.title_en: Resonant Multiphoton Conversion Mediated by a Shared Vibration in Cavity QED
papers.abstract_en: We show that a vibration shared by two emitter subensembles can jointly establish multiphoton resonance and constructive interference among the virtual exchange pathways responsible for coherent conversion. For opposite displacements with an integer magnitude ratio $r\geq2$, the displacements induced by $r$ excitations in the less displaced subensemble and one in the other cancel exactly, a condition we call displacement neutrality. When the emitter and cavity frequencies match, the resulting composite is resonant with $r+1$ cavity photons, while the vibration-mediated cross interaction makes the conversion pathways add constructively, establishing a direct relation between the displacement ratio and the conversion order. In contrast, independent vibrations can be tuned to the same resonance, but their conversion pathways cancel at leading order, demonstrating that energy resonance alone does not guarantee coherent conversion. For $r=2$, this conversion suppresses three-photon coincidences while leaving the two-photon statistics nearly Poissonian. In the weak-driving limit, interference can also screen the two-photon correlations at all delays from the relative direction of the displacements, whereas the three-photon statistics remain sensitive to it. Because both resonant states leave the vibration undisplaced, their coherence is protected from direct dephasing by the shared vibration, leaving emitter dephasing as the tighter constraint. These results identify relative vibrational displacements as a means of controlling coherent multiphoton conversion and its noise response.

papers.title_en: Two-qubit binegativity can increase under local amplitude damping
papers.abstract_en: It has been conjectured that the binegativity of two-qubit states is an entanglement monotone. We present a full-rank state as a counterexample: applying amplitude damping to only one of the qubits can increase the binegativity of the state. The output state remains full rank, and the amount of increase can be calculated exactly. In addition, we construct a family of counterexamples that vary continuously with a parameter. In the corresponding one-way local operations and classical communication protocol, the probability-weighted average of the binegativity over the branches after the local measurement is also higher than that of the initial state.

papers.title_en: Near-exact Upper Confidence Limits for Axion Haloscopes
papers.abstract_en: The data acquisition of axion haloscopes commonly implements sequential adaptive frequency scans. We present a method to calculate likelihood-based upper confidence limits on axion-photon coupling under this circumstance. We compare the likelihood-based method conceptually and quantitatively with tailor-made methods, i.e. the one proposed by Brubaker et al. (Geometric) and its upgrade the Bayesian Power-Measured (BPM) framework proposed by Palken et al. We find that the likelihood method yields average upper limits that are significantly more constraining than those obtained from these methods. For example, expected constraints improve by a factor of 1.4 as compared with the current state of the art when applied to projections for the ALPHA Plasma-haloscope. We further clarify the statistical basis for the Geometric and BPM methods. In particular, we point out the correspondence of BPM to e-values, proposed as an alternative to conventional p-values in statistics.

papers.title_en: MATHUSLA: A Proposed Long-Lived Particle Detector for High-Luminosity LHC
papers.abstract_en: Beyond the Standard Model long-lived particles (LLPs) appear in many theories that address fundamental open questions, such as the hierarchy problem and the nature of dark matter. The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) may be producing copious numbers of neutral LLPs with masses above a GeV, only for these sneaky particles to escape the main detectors without being spotted. To fill this gap, we have proposed MATHUSLA (MAssive Timing Hodoscope for Ultra-Stable neutraL pArticles), which would be constructed on the surface above CMS and would take data during High-Luminosity LHC operations. The detector would be composed of several layers of solid plastic scintillator threaded with wavelength-shifting fibers that connect to silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs), and would monitor an empty, air-filled decay volume. The Conceptual Design Report (CDR) published in 2025 sets out a benchmark geometry of 40m x 40m x 16m, with a modular detector construction scheme that would allow data collection to begin as soon as the first module is installed. This proceeding documents the results of more detailed studies conducted since the CDR on the detector's potential location, mechanical engineering of modules, data acquisition system, cosmic ray backgrounds, event selection criteria, and trigger algorithms.

papers.title_en: Minimal ancilla for boosting type-I photonic fusion
papers.abstract_en: Fusion gates enable the creation of large entangled photonic states for linear-optical quantum computing and communication protocols. However, their success probability is limited to $1/2$ without additional photonic resources. Previous schemes for boosting type-I fusion have used four ancillary single photons or a two-qubit Bell state, whose preparation is probabilistic and resource intensive. Here we propose a boosted type-I fusion gate using only two independent ancillary single photons and no entangled ancillary input. It achieves a direct success probability of $5/8$, matching that of the previous four-single-photon proposal while using half as many ancillary photons. The circuit is predominantly passive, with a single active element that applies a phase shift or swaps two modes according to intermediate photodetection outcomes. Unlike the previous schemes, successful outputs occupy fixed modes and require no further conditional output routing. In particular, we show that the gate is more robust to heralded ancillary-photon loss than previously proposed boosted gates and reduces the average number of single photons required to generate a six-qubit ring graph state by more than $4.6\%$ compared with other type-I schemes. It therefore offers a resource-efficient primitive for scalable fusion-based photonic quantum information processing.

papers.title_en: Pauli-ball discrepancy and stability of quantum codes
papers.abstract_en: The Pauli-ball discrepancy, a quadratic discrepancy summed over all error radii, measures how uniformly the Pauli error images of a $K$-dimensional quantum code cover the $d$-dimensional Hilbert space. At parameters attaining equality in the quantum Singleton bound with minimum code distance $\geq3$, or in the one-error Hamming bound with prime-power local dimension, the discrepancy of every projector of the prescribed rank equals an explicit benchmark plus an exact nonnegative remainder, which vanishes precisely for pure quantum maximum-distance-separable codes and nondegenerate perfect codes, respectively. For a Pauli ball of radius $e$ below half the target distance and size $V_e$, this remainder linearly bounds the squared Hilbert--Schmidt distance of the error-image Gram matrix from the identity. When $KV_e\leq d$, it linearly bounds the diamond error and entanglement infidelity of a noise-independent polar recovery under any noise in that ball's span. For five qubits, we obtain the sharp rank-two Gram constant and exact logical channels of rotated codes attaining this linear order in diamond error. For pure states, the discrepancy equals a pure-state benchmark plus a positive weighted sum of marginal-purity defects, so absolutely maximally entangled states, when they exist, are exactly the minimizers.

papers.title_en: High-order temperature fluctuations in hot and dense QCD matter from multi-charge holography
papers.abstract_en: We investigate temperature cumulants from second to sixth order across the QCD phase diagram using a lattice-calibrated multi-charge Einstein--Maxwells--dilaton model under heavy-ion charge constraints. Near the model's critical end point at $(μ_B,T)\simeq(547,112)$~MeV, the enhanced heat capacity produces a local suppression of the temperature variance. The higher-order cumulants develop sign reversals on the high-temperature side of the transition, with the onset moving to lower baryon chemical potentials as the order increases. Ratios of different cumulant orders provide a consistency check of the expected mean-field critical behavior. At fixed chemical potentials, their limits on both sides of the critical point agree with the predictions for the critical-isotherm exponent $δ=3$. The freeze-out analysis reveals nonmonotonic collision-energy dependence that need not be accompanied by sign reversals. On a representative trajectory, the variance reaches a local minimum near $\sqrt{s_{NN}}\simeq6$~GeV, with its position and depth depending on the freeze-out path. Temperature cumulants probe the thermal response and its critical scaling, providing information complementary to conserved-charge fluctuations for exploring the QCD phase diagram.

papers.title_en: Emergent Recursive Kernels in Quantum Reservoir Computing
papers.abstract_en: Learning with a quantum reservoir can be far simpler than simulating its dynamics. We show that a quantum reservoir governed by a fixed evolution, consisting of an input coupling followed by an independently sampled Haar unitary, admits an exact recursive kernel in the large-dimension limit at fixed history length. Memory orthogonality and factorization of propagated overlaps reduce each kernel evaluation to a scalar recurrence, linear in history length and independent of reservoir size. We establish self-averaging around this limit and connect the kernel coefficients to out-of-time-ordered correlators. Our analysis of finite-dimensional effects shows that the computational simplicity of the Haar kernel does not come at the expense of expressive power. Moreover, we demonstrate how the kernel can be tuned for different learning tasks by adjusting properties such as memory retention and temporal interaction order. On the NARMA10 benchmark, the tuned kernel achieves lower prediction error than the tested Ising and Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev reservoirs.

papers.title_en: Exact Identification of Quantum Correlations in the Minimal Bell Scenario
papers.abstract_en: Bell nonlocality places the long-standing philosophical disputes over the nature of quantum theory on a mathematically rigorous, experimentally testable footing, positioning quantum mechanics between local realism and the most general no-signaling theories. Yet the precise quantum boundary has remained elusive even in the minimal Bell scenario, where the extreme points generating the set are known. Here we characterize this boundary through a computable necessary and sufficient criterion: a correlation is quantum if and only if it can be decomposed into an extreme quantum correlation and a classical correlation. The criterion follows from our proof that every Bell functional exhibiting quantum advantage admits a unique quantum maximizer. We further classify the finitely many maximal-face structures containing each nonlocal exposed point according to their local deterministic vertices. By sharply distinguishing physically realizable correlations from nonphysical ones, these results resolve a long-standing open problem and provide a new foundation for identifying the principles underlying quantum theory and determining the ultimate information-theoretic limits of quantum correlations.

papers.title_en: Ancilla-free optimal quantum adder
papers.abstract_en: We construct an exact $n$-bit quantum adder with $O(n)$ gates and $O(\log n)$ depth that requires no ancillary qubits. The circuit uses only $X$, CNOT, and Toffoli gates under all-to-all connectivity and is classically reversible. Our construction accelerates the controlled ladder underlying addition. Grouping the data into blocks and use existing control qubits as conditional workspace gives a recursive construction with $O(n\log\log n)$ gates and $O(\log n)$ depth. We then coordinate inter-block propagation via two short-path forest operations to cut the per-block workspace requirement, yielding a nonrecursive implementation with $O(n)$ gates. Both the gate count and circuit depth are asymptotically optimal.

papers.title_en: Pion vector form factor from LapH-smeared currents in lattice QCD
papers.abstract_en: We explore a method to extract pion vector form factor from three-point functions using currents constructed from LapH-smeared quark fields. LapH employs the low eigenmodes of the Laplacian Heaviside operator on the lattice to smear out the quark fields in spatial directions. The LapH-smeared quark propagator retains all symmetry properties of the original one and can be re-used to construct correlation functions at a reduced cost, with equal treatment of connected and disconnected diagrams. The calculations are performed on a two-flavor dynamical nHYP-smeared ensemble on the $24^3\times 48$ lattice at a spacing of 0.12 fm and pion mass of 315 MeV. We show that an extrapolation in the number of low eigenmodes in the LapH subspace can reproduce the same form factor computed from the conventional SST method with point source, sink, and current. The study opens up the possibility of applying LapH-smeared currents to extract hadron form factors and polarizabilities including disconnected diagrams.

papers.title_en: Bosonic Loss Codes with Bounded Occupation
papers.abstract_en: We study Fock-state codes on $q$ bosonic modes, with total excitation $N$ and at most $B$ excitations per mode, that exactly correct every pattern of at most $δN$ photon losses, for $q$ proportional to $N$. For every fixed cap $B$ and every ratio $q/N>1/B$, we prove explicit achievable rates, positive for all sufficiently small $δ>0$, in logical qubits per excitation. At $B=2$ and $q=N$, the rate is positive for every $δ<0.1355$ and is about $0.281$ at $δ=0.1$, compared with the previously established exact-code qutrit rate of about $0.275$. We also give an explicit upper bound on the dimension of every such exact code, including degenerate codes. For the pure-loss channel truncated to at most $δN$ losses and renormalized, we obtain approximate codes with exponentially small worst-case error. When the loss probability is positive and at most $1/(B+1)$, they improve our positive exact-code rate bounds; at $B=2$, $q=N$, and loss probability $0.1$, they remain positive up to $δ\approx0.158$.

papers.title_en: Real-Time Correlation of Relaxation, Dephasing, and Two-level System Dynamics in Transmon Qubits
papers.abstract_en: Materials improvements in transmon qubits have yielded remarkable advances in qubit lifetimes (T1)and coherence times (T2). However, state-of-the-art superconducting qubits experience temporal fluctuations in their performance, which limit gate fidelities and quantum processor performance. We observe correlated increases in qubit relaxation and dephasing rates that last for minutes to hours, which we call T1 and T2 excursions. Using interleaved lifetime and coherence time measurements, noise spectroscopy, and two-level-system (TLS) spectroscopy, we find that these excursions are caused by single or few strongly-coupled TLS defects that spectrally diffuse into resonance with the qubit frequency. Our measurement protocol provides a powerful tool for understanding the noise sources that cause temporal fluctuations in superconducting qubit performance.

papers.title_en: QQLink: A Declarative Framework for Multi-QPU Quantum Workflow Orchestration
papers.abstract_en: Distributed quantum protocols require measurement outcomes produced at one node to control operations at another. We present QQLink, a programming and orchestration layer that expresses these dependencies in a single program, using workflow nodes, deferred measurement references, and declared entanglement, and derives the cross-node coordination automatically. Its planner constructs a provably acyclic dependency graph in time linear in the total size of the instructions' qubit footprints. The same programs execute through simulator backends or are lowered to dynamic circuits on partitioned quantum hardware. We evaluate seven protocol workflows. Exhaustive feedforward-branch tests on the simulator runtime path, over tomographically complete input sets, yield output-state infidelities of at most $5\times10^{-12}$ and no incorrect classical outputs, and replaying every plan in random topological orders leaves each final state unchanged. Separate executor processes run the plans with delayed messages, with the joint quantum state held by a centralized simulation service. Every run with the full plan is correct, and removing required cross-node dependencies causes protocol failures. The lowered circuits match hand-written implementations of the same construction in two-qubit gate and conditional-block counts. Runs on two IBM Heron processors, each partitioned into virtual QPUs, demonstrate same-chip execution in two sessions a week apart. The runs also show large variation between sessions and losses beyond what calibration-derived noise models predict. Coherence-sensitive checks do not establish coherent Toffoli operation or preservation of the intended repetition-code superposition. These results support QQLink's workflow semantics on the tested execution paths and identify limits of the current hardware realization; execution across physically networked QPUs remains future work.

papers.title_en: Higher Order OTOCs in Chaotic Quantum Maps: Ruelle-Pollicott Resonances and Asymptotic Freeness
papers.abstract_en: Out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) measure the scrambling of information and are a powerful diagnostic of chaos. In chaotic quantum systems with a classical analog, their relaxation towards equilibrium is dictated by the classical Ruelle--Pollicott resonances. We investigate higher-order OTOCs in quantum maps, prototypical one-body systems with a classical limit showing all the essential features of chaotic dynamics. We demonstrate numerically that in the intermediate-time regime they decay exponentially at a rate that depends only on the parity of the order: odd-order OTOCs decay at the same rate as classical correlations, given by the leading Ruelle--Pollicott resonance, and even-order ones at twice that rate. Both are far slower than the naive expectation, under which the rate would grow in proportion to the order. We then mimic the effect of an environment by defining a coarse-grained superoperator whose effect is to introduce decoherence into the system, and find that the expected proportionality between rate and order is thereby restored. Finally, we show that at long times each higher-order OTOC becomes dominated by a single free cumulant, whose saturation value falls off inversely with the dimension of the Hilbert space, signalling the emergence of asymptotic freeness and highlighting the relevance of free probability theory as a framework for the study of quantum chaos.

papers.title_en: Model-Uncertainty-Aware Digital Twins for Non-Markovian Quantum Repeater Memories
papers.abstract_en: Quantum-repeater controllers need reliable estimates of stored entanglement as adjacent links are generated. Fixed exponential lifetimes miss non-Markovian revivals, while complex surrogates are unnecessary when the microscopic family is known. We present QMemTwin, a physics-constrained digital twin that accounts for model uncertainty. It calibrates a bank of contractive passive state-space models, combines their amplitudes with finite-sample-corrected Akaike weights, and abstains when temporal-holdout data indicate unsupported dynamics. Passivity guarantees a completely positive, trace-preserving amplitude-damping channel for each candidate and their convex amplitude average. We evaluate [N cases] synthetic memories: [N supported] supported passive time-invariant cases and [N structural] nonstationary structural-shift cases. In the matched one-pseudomode regime, the correctly specified one-pseudomode fit performs best. Across [N unknown] supported cases with uncertain families, QMemTwin reduces population RMSE by [population reduction]% and Bell-fidelity RMSE by [Bell reduction]% relative to the two-pseudomode model; both paired effects remain significant after Holm correction. The flexible passive model has a slightly lower mean error for unknown families but is statistically indistinguishable from QMemTwin and loses accuracy in the matched regime. The temporal-holdout gate detects [detection]% of structural shifts, with [false alarm]% false alarms on supported families and AUROC [AUC]. In 2-, 4-, and 8-link repeater chains, the mixed cohort shows no significant 8-link goodput gain. A predeclared high-backflow stress cohort yields an 8-link goodput gain of [goodput gain]% over the two-pseudomode model, with paired p = [p value]. These results favor using a known family when available, accounting for model uncertainty otherwise and abstaining on unsupported dynamics.

papers.title_en: Lévy-stable pion emission sources in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV from the vHLLE+SMASH hybrid model
papers.abstract_en: Revealing the space-time evolution of the quark-gluon plasma created in heavy-ion collisions is a central challenge, as this information is encoded in the properties of particles emitted at freeze-out. We reconstruct the pion emission source in Au+Au collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 200 GeV (0-5% centrality), simulated with the vHLLE+SMASH hybrid framework, which combines a Glauber Monte Carlo initial state, (3+1)-dimensional viscous hydrodynamics, and a hadronic afterburner describing resonance decays and hadronic rescattering. Hanbury Brown-Twiss (HBT) interferometry is used to characterize identical-pion pair sources, which can also be reconstructed directly from the last scattering points of final-state particles in simulations. The projected pair-separation distributions in the Bertsch-Pratt out, side, and long directions are analyzed using a three-dimensional Levy-stable parameterization. Over the investigated fit range, extending to approximately 100 fm, a single Levy-stable function provides a satisfactory description of the distributions. The extracted Levy index, alpha approximately 1.5-1.6, is below the Gaussian value of 2 and increases slowly with transverse mass mT. At larger pair separations, the total source deviates from the fitted distribution, consistent with a halo contribution from long-lived resonance decays. Short-lived resonance decays and hadronic rescattering may contribute to the non-Gaussian shape through the Levy-walk phenomenon. The HBT radii Rout, Rside, and Rlong decrease with mT, qualitatively consistent with collective expansion. These results demonstrate the utility of Levy-stable femtoscopy for connecting hadronic-stage dynamics in hybrid simulations with experimentally accessible observables.

papers.title_en: Nucleon tomography from a calibrated diquark spectator model
papers.abstract_en: Generalized parton distributions (GPDs) provide a unified description of the longitudinal-momentum and transverse spatial structure of the nucleon. We calculate the twist-2 vector GPDs $H^{q}$ and $E^{q}$ in a spectator model containing both scalar and axial-vector diquark configurations. A central new result is the explicit analytic expression for the axial-vector-diquark contribution to the helicity-flip GPD $E^{q}$. To regulate the transverse-momentum integrations while retaining a physically sensible dependence on the momentum transfer, we introduce a momentum-transfer-dependent quasi-hard cutoff. The model parameters are determined through two complementary calibrations: one using proton observables only and another simultaneously including proton and neutron observables. Electromagnetic moments and radii, together with selected constraints on gravitational form factors, determine the quark and diquark masses, the relative scalar and axial-vector contributions, and the transverse-momentum scale. The two calibrations yield compatible parameter ranges, while the inclusion of neutron observables reduces the parameter uncertainties and more strongly constrains the flavor structure. From the resulting zero-skewness GPDs $H^{u,d}(x,0,t)$ and $E^{u,d}(x,0,t)$, we calculate the valence-quark PDFs and the impact-parameter distributions of unpolarized up and down quarks in both unpolarized and transversely polarized nucleons. The transverse distributions exhibit the expected localization of large-$x$ quarks near the transverse center of momentum and a flavor-dependent distortion when the nucleon is transversely polarized. Our results provide a unified phenomenological description of the longitudinal-momentum and transverse-position structure of valence quarks in the nucleon.

papers.title_en: Quantum Anomaly Detection in network traffic using Variational Quantum Classifiers
papers.abstract_en: The increasingly complex cybersecurity landscape requires more advanced network anomaly detection systems. Although, classical machine learning models are known to be effective, they reach computational bottlenecks when processing high-dimensional data.
